status.en: 160 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 160 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen abducted six mourners on a Benue highway and later abandoned a corpse, while separate gunmen killed a pastor, three others and injured eight in a community raid in Benue. In Kaduna a fresh attack left two dead and 20 people kidnapped, and security agencies later rescued eight abducted victims, while bandits killed a pregnant woman, a soldier and a hunter and abducted fifteen people in Taraba. A suspect was arrested for the attack on Peter Obi’s convoy in Calabar. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Skytevåpnede menn bortførte seks sørgende på en motorvei i Benue og etterpå forlot et lik, mens andre skytevåpnede menn drepte en pastor, tre andre og såret åtte i et raid i et lokalsamfunn i Benue. I Kaduna førte et nytt angrep til to døde og 20 kidnappede, og sikkerhetsmyndighetene reddet senere åtte bortførte personer, mens banditter drepte en gravid kvinne, en soldat og en jeger og bortførte femten personer i Taraba. En mistenkt ble arrestert for angrepet på Peter Obis følge i Calabar. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
